g.text: For the ESP32-S3, the USB peripheral is available, allowing you to flash

g.desc: For the ESP32-S3, the USB peripheral is available, allowing you to flash

g.text: the binaries without the need for an external USB-to-UART bridge.

g.desc: the binaries without the need for an external USB-to-UART bridge.

g.text: The USB on the ESP32-S3 uses the GPIO20 for D+ and GPIO19 for D-.

g.desc: The USB on the ESP32-S3 uses the GPIO20 for D+ and GPIO19 for D-.

g.text: If you are flashing for the first time, you need to get the ESP32-S3

g.desc: If you are flashing for the first time, you need to get the ESP32-S3

g.text: into the download mode manually. To do so, press and hold the BOOT button

g.desc: into the download mode manually. To do so, press and hold the BOOT button

g.text: and then press the RESET button once. After that release the BOOT button.

g.desc: and then press the RESET button once. After that release the BOOT button.

g.text: This PinHeader Is Excluded from Board.

g.desc: This PinHeader Is Excluded from Board.

g.text: The spi_master driver uses the following terms:

g.desc: The spi_master driver uses the following terms:

g.text: Host: The SPI peripheral inside the ESP32 initiating the SPI

g.desc: Host: The SPI peripheral inside the ESP32 initiating the SPI

g.text: transmissions. One of SPI, HSPI or VSPI. (For now, only HSPI

g.desc: transmissions. One of SPI, HSPI or VSPI. (For now, only HSPI

g.text: or VSPI are actually supported in the driver; it will support

g.desc: or VSPI are actually supported in the driver; it will support

g.text: all 3 peripherals somewhere in the future.)

g.desc: all 3 peripherals somewhere in the future.)

g.text: Bus: The SPI bus, common to all SPI devices connected to one

g.desc: Bus: The SPI bus, common to all SPI devices connected to one

g.text: host. In general the bus consists of the miso, mosi, sclk

g.desc: host. In general the bus consists of the miso, mosi, sclk

g.text: and optionally quadwp and quadhd signals. The SPI slaves are

g.desc: and optionally quadwp and quadhd signals. The SPI slaves are

g.text: connected to these signals in parallel.

g.desc: connected to these signals in parallel.

g.text: - miso - Also known as q, this is the input of the serial stream

g.desc: - miso - Also known as q, this is the input of the serial stream

g.text: - mosi - Also known as d, this is the output of the serial stream

g.desc: - mosi - Also known as d, this is the output of the serial stream

g.text: - sclk - Clock signal. Each data bit is clocked out or in on the

g.desc: - sclk - Clock signal. Each data bit is clocked out or in on the

g.text: positive or negative edge of this signal

g.desc: positive or negative edge of this signal

g.text: - quadwp - Write Protect signal. Only used for 4-bit (qio/qout)

g.desc: - quadwp - Write Protect signal. Only used for 4-bit (qio/qout)

g.text: - quadhd - Hold signal. Only used for 4-bit (qio/qout) transactions.

g.desc: - quadhd - Hold signal. Only used for 4-bit (qio/qout) transactions.

g.text: Device: A SPI slave. Each SPI slave has its own chip select (CS) line,

g.desc: Device: A SPI slave. Each SPI slave has its own chip select (CS) line,

g.text: which is made active when a transmission to/from the SPI slave occurs.

g.desc: which is made active when a transmission to/from the SPI slave occurs.

g.text: Transaction: One instance of CS going active, data transfer from and/or

g.desc: Transaction: One instance of CS going active, data transfer from and/or

g.text: to a device happening, and CS going inactive again. Transactions are

g.desc: to a device happening, and CS going inactive again. Transactions are

g.text: atomic, as in they will never be interrupted by another transaction.

g.desc: atomic, as in they will never be interrupted by another transaction.
